title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors versus placebo in patients with major depressive disorder. A systematic review with meta-analysis and Trial Sequential Analysis
authors: Jakobsen JC, Katakam KK, Schou A, Hellmuth SG, Stallknecht SE, Leth-Møller K, et al.
population: 131 randomised placebo-controlled trials of SSRIs in adults with major depressive disorder, published and unpublished, searched to January 2016
funder: The Copenhagen Trial Unit, Centre for Clinical Intervention Research, Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark, provided economic support for JCJ, KKK, JL and CG. Otherwise, we have received no funding.
authorConflicts: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.
result: All trials were at high risk of bias. Hamilton score fell by 1.94 points more than placebo (95% CI -2.50 to -1.37; 49 trials), below the authors' 3-point threshold for clinical significance; risk of no remission RR 0.88 (0.84 to 0.91; 34 trials). Serious adverse events (death, life threat, disability, hospital admission) in 239 of 8242 (2.7%) on SSRIs against 106 of 4956 (2.1%) on placebo, OR 1.37 (1.08 to 1.75; 44 trials), 31 against 22 per 1000, number needed to harm 138. Almost no data on suicidal behaviour, quality of life or long-term effects.
